question: Which postulate of Dalton’s atomic theory reflects the Law of Conservation of Mass?

options.text: Atoms cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Atoms of different elements have different masses and properties.
Atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios to form compounds.
All matter is made up of indivisible particles called atoms.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Atoms cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The statement "**Atoms cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction**" aligns directly with the **Law of Conservation of Mass**, which states that **mass in a closed system remains constant** during a chemical reaction.
 
• Dalton's atomic theory postulated that **atoms are indestructible and unchangeable**. This principle ensures that the total mass of reactants and products in a chemical reaction remains equal.
 
• The **Law of Conservation of Mass** was formulated by **Antoine Lavoisier**, who demonstrated that matter cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed.
 
• This concept is fundamental in chemical equations, where the **number of atoms** of each element must be balanced on both sides of the reaction.
 
• Dalton's idea strengthened the understanding of **chemical processes**, emphasizing that no atom vanishes or appears during reactions, ensuring the conservation of matter.
 
• This principle forms the basis of stoichiometry, which deals with the calculation of reactants and products in chemical reactions.
 
• It is particularly significant in industries such as **pharmaceuticals, petrochemicals, and material science**, where precise chemical reactions are crucial.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atoms of different elements have different masses and properties.**__

 __
 
• This postulate highlights the **unique identity of each element**, as the atoms of one element differ in **mass, size, and chemical properties** from atoms of other elements.
 
• It explains why different elements exhibit distinct behaviors, forming compounds with specific properties.
 
• This principle is crucial in understanding the **Periodic Table**, where elements are arranged based on their atomic properties.
 
 
 
• **Atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios to form compounds.**__
 __
 
• This postulate is related to the **Law of Definite Proportions**, which states that chemical compounds are composed of elements in fixed ratios by mass.
 
• For example, water (H₂O) always consists of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
 
• It forms the foundation for understanding **chemical bonding** and molecular structures.
 
 
 
• **All matter is made up of indivisible particles called atoms.**__
 
 
• This postulate introduced the idea that **atoms are the basic building blocks of matter**.
 
• Though later developments in science showed that atoms can be divided into subatomic particles, the concept remains fundamental to understanding matter's structure.
 
• It is crucial in the fields of **physics, chemistry, and material science** for studying the properties and behavior of matter.
